lede: You have a vault that seals evidence no one can open alone. This is how you stand it up — and prove it works — in four commands: init, enroll, drill, doctor.

commands.name: init
commands.what: Pins the device identity in the (encrypted) kernel database and opens an n-of-m setup draft. Writes no quorum policy yet — an empty roster is not a valid gate. Idempotent: re-running reports where you are, it never clobbers.

flags.desc: how many trustees must approve to break the glass
how many trustees you plan to enroll in total
the device seed (also DEVICE_KEY_SEED) — opens the encrypted DB

commands.name: trustee enroll
commands.one_line: Add one trustee — import a key, or mint one.
commands.what: Adds one trustee to the draft. Import a public key a trustee generated themselves (--public-key), or mint a fresh Ed25519 keypair for them (--generate) — the signing key is written at mode 0600 to hand over. Rejects duplicate ids and reused keys up front. The real quorum policy commits automatically, once, when the roster is complete — earlier enrollments only edit the draft.

flags.desc: a short, unique label for this trustee
import an existing 32-byte Ed25519 public key
mint a keypair; write the signing key (0600) to hand over
the device seed (also DEVICE_KEY_SEED) — required, opens the encrypted DB

commands.name: drill
commands.what: Runs the entire request → approve → authorize → seal → unseal path in a throwaway sandbox — a temp database, a temp vault and ephemeral trustee keys, all discarded afterward. It touches nothing real. Proves break-glass actually works on this build/host before you need it at 3 a.m., and lets trustees practice with zero risk. Exits non-zero if any step fails.

commands.name: doctor
commands.one_line: Is this vault set up correctly? Gate a deploy on it.
commands.what: A read-only health check. Reports the quorum policy (n-of-m, every trustee key well-formed), whether the device identity is pinned AND matches the supplied seed, and the vault master key's state — including a loud reminder that the master key is plaintext on disk (the honest state until hardware-backed keys land). Exits non-zero on any problem, so it can gate a deploy in a script or CI.

flags.desc: verifies the seed derives the pinned identity

concepts.title: A draft, kept apart from the gate
concepts.blurb: Enrollment fills a draft roster — a plain file next to the database (<db>.setup-draft.json), holding only public keys and counts, no secrets. It is deliberately separate from the committed quorum policy, because the kernel rejects an empty or partial roster by design (Invariant V). A half-finished setup can never be mistaken for a live gate.

concepts.title: It goes live when the roster is complete
concepts.blurb: The real policy commits automatically, once, when the m-th trustee is enrolled. Committing earlier — at the threshold — would have made every later enrollment a silent rewrite of a LIVE policy, exactly the roster-mutation path the quorum gate exists to close (Invariant V). The commit runs the kernel's own validate(), so the gate is never partial and reused keys are refused.

concepts.title: Mint or import — your call
concepts.blurb: A trustee can generate their own key and send you only the public half (import), or you can mint one for them. A minted signing key is written at mode 0600 to hand over — it is the one secret in the whole flow; the draft never holds it.

concepts.title: Rehearse before you trust it
concepts.blurb: drill runs the full break-glass in a throwaway sandbox — real crypto, real quorum counting, real single-use token burn — and proves recovery works before an incident, with zero risk to your vault. Then doctor gates the deploy.

concepts.title: Honest about what isn't hardened yet
concepts.blurb: doctor says out loud that the master key is plaintext on disk — the honest state until hardware-backed keys land (v1.1) — and fails hard if that key is readable beyond its owner or if the supplied seed doesn't match the pinned identity.
